newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso firmer on long bond, inflation hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso firmer on long bond, inflation hopes.

text.p: The Mexican peso opened marginally stronger on Thursday after tracking the U.S. long bond and on a favorable outlook for inflation data expected later in the day.
"The peso is very strong; just look at the long bond and the local bourse," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart opened 0.2 and 0.7 of a centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.8260/7.8310 and 7.8180/7.8230 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had meanwhile begun the session 2.3 centavos firmer at 7.8130/7.8180 per dollar to line up with other contacts after their early close the day before.
The U.S. long bond was up 5/32 to yield 6.42 percent, while the Mexican bourse had advanced 25.40 points to 4,767.52 points.
Dealers said they were hopeful inflation data would point the way to further cuts in domestic interest rates.
A Reuters survey of 12 Mexico City financial firms showed they forecast an average rise of 0.47 percent for the Consumer Price Index between July 1-15.
